title: Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib, Anandpur Sahib
content:
Introduction

Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib is one of the five sacred Takhts of Sikhism, located in the holy town of Anandpur Sahib, Punjab. This revered site holds immense religious, historical, and spiritual significance as it is the place where Guru Gobind Singh Ji founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699. Surrounded by the scenic Shivalik Hills, the Takht stands as a symbol of courage, equality, and devotion.

Historical Significance

Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib marks the historic event of Baisakhi 1699, when Guru Gobind Singh Ji initiated the Panj Pyare and laid the foundation of the Khalsa. From this sacred place, Sikhs were given a new identity based on justice, bravery, and selfless service. The Takht also served as an important center for Sikh military and spiritual activities during the Mughal period.

Religious Importance

As one of the five Takhts, Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib functions as a supreme seat of Sikh authority. Important religious decisions, ceremonies, and gatherings take place here. Thousands of devotees visit daily to offer prayers and seek blessings, especially during Hola Mohalla and Baisakhi, which are celebrated with great enthusiasm.

Architecture of Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib

The architecture of Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib reflects traditional Sikh design blended with modern elements. The white marble structure, elegant domes, and spacious prayer halls create a peaceful and divine atmosphere. Inside the Takht, sacred weapons and historical artifacts associated with Guru Gobind Singh Ji are preserved, adding to its spiritual aura.

Location & How to Reach

Visitor Guidelines

  •  Dress modestly and cover your head
  • Remove shoes before entering
  • Maintain silence and respect religious practices
  • Langar (free community meal) is available for all visitors

faqs.question: Where is Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib located?
faqs.answer: Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib is located in Anandpur Sahib, Rupnagar district, Punjab, India.

faqs.question: Why is Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib important?
faqs.answer: It is the birthplace of the Khalsa Panth, established by Guru Gobind Singh Ji in 1699, and is one of the five sacred Takhts of Sikhism.

faqs.question: Are non-Sikhs allowed to visit Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib?
faqs.answer: Yes, people of all religions are welcome. Visitors must follow basic Gurudwara etiquette.

faqs.question: Is Langar available at Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib?
faqs.answer: Yes, free Langar is served daily to all visitors, irrespective of caste, creed, or religion.

faqs.question: What are the nearest attractions to visit?
faqs.answer: Nearby attractions include Virasat-e-Khalsa Museum, Anandgarh Sahib, Qila Lohgarh, and Charan Ganga Stadium.
